_note: Baseline for the behavioural tier. UNMEASURED: every statistic below is null on purpose. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is now configured (it was the blocker this note used to name, issue #171), and the first graded run taken after it -- 31229964963 -- still does not qualify: it answered all 12 with_skill executions with claude-opus-5[1m] and all 12 without_skill executions with claude-haiku-4-5, so its +0.13 delta measures the models rather than the plugin. The runner now refuses such a benchmark and skills-eval.yml pins --model, so the next run is seedable. Seeding this with a plausible number would give #173's regression alarm something to compare against that nobody measured, which is the failure mode CLAUDE.md's readout section spends a page on: reporting health from absent evidence. The shape is aggregate_benchmark.py's output so a real run drops straight in.
comparability: A BASELINE IS ONLY COMPARABLE AGAINST RUNS OF THE SAME MODEL. metadata.executor_model and metadata.analyzer_model below record which model produced these numbers; the Aggregate step in skills-eval.yml stamps them from what the runner observed on the wire, because the `model` dispatch input is blank on any run that took the CLI default and aggregate_benchmark.py otherwise writes the literal string "<model-name>" (issue #203). Compare a run against this baseline only when those fields match. A model change moves the pass rate for reasons that have nothing to do with the skills, and #173's regression alarm reading a mismatched pair would report a skill regression that is really a model upgrade — attributing the delta to the wrong cause. When the models differ, the right move is to re-seed the baseline on the new model, not to interpret the delta.
how_to_seed: 1. Confirm ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set on the repository. It is, as of 2026-08-08 -- the check is that the steps gated on steps.key.outputs.present in skills-eval.yml actually execute.
2. Run the 'Skills eval (behavioural)' workflow via workflow_dispatch with runs=3. Three runs is the minimum that yields a stddev worth reading.

3. Leave the `model` input at its default. Blank lets each session choose, and in run 31229964963 that put the two arms on two different models; the runner refuses the resulting benchmark, so a blank run is a wasted 40 minutes rather than a bad baseline.

4. Read the 'Probe the session shape' step before anything else. It is the #226 guard: with_skill must register the plugin's commands and the control must register none, or the run measures nothing whatever its numbers say.
5. Download the behavioural-benchmark artifact and merge its measured fields over this file -- keep `comparability`, `how_to_seed` and this note, which the artifact does not carry.
6. Read the stddev before trusting the mean. Per evals/README.md a wide-variance case is a defect in the case, not a finding about the skill -- fix the case before it becomes a baseline.
7. Check that metadata.executor_model is a real model name, is not null, and names exactly ONE model. A comma-joined pair means the arms diverged and the delta is uninterpretable.
